header.running_head: 3. The Rights and Duties of Muslims

blocks.arabic_text: قَالَ: فَلَمَّا وَلَّيْتُ دَعَانِيْ فَقَالَ: مَاهُوَ اِلَّا مَارَاَيْتَ غَيْرَ اَنِّيْ لَا اَجِدُ فِيْ نَفْسِيْ لِاَحَدٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِيْنَ غَشًّا، وَلَا اَحْسِدُ اَحَدًا عَلَي خَيْرٍ اَعْطَاهُ اللهُ اِيّاهُ، فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللهِ: هذِهِ الَّتِيْ بَلَغَتْ بِكَ وَهِيَ الَّذِيْ لَا نُطِيْقُ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه احمد والبزار بنحوه ورجال احمد رجال الصحيح مجمع الزوائد:١٥٠/٨
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Anas ibn Malik (RA) narrates: “We were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when the Prophet ﷺ said, “A man from the people of Jannah will now come to you.” After a little while, an Ansari Sahabi came, with the water of Wudu dripping from his beard and carrying his sandals in his left hand. On the second day too, Rasulullah ﷺ said the same as he had said on the first day. Then the same Ansari Sahabi (RA) came this time too, in the same state in which he had come on the first day. On the third day Rasulullah ﷺ again said the same thing. The same Ansari Sahabi (RA) came in the same state in which he had come on the first day. When the Prophet ﷺ got up and left (that gathering), Hazrat Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) followed that Ansari and said, “A disagreement has arisen between me and my father, so I have sworn that I will not go to him for three days; if you are willing, please let me stay with you for three days.” And he said, “Very well.” I spent three nights with him, and I did not see him get up at night to worship. But whenever he woke during the night, or turned over in bed, he would do the Dhikr of Allah Ta'ala. He would say “Allahu Akbar”. In this same state he would get up from bed to pray Fajr. I saw one more thing in him: I heard nothing from him except good words. When the three nights had passed, I considered his deeds to be very ordinary
